literature_notes: All five ledger lines were evaluated. L1, L2, and L3 describe C-terminal HA or FLAG tags on full-length membrane-anchored MOG. The canonical topology places the C-terminus (residue 247) firmly in the intracellular region (230–247); these tags are therefore intracellular and cannot serve as extracellular surface-tag sites. L4 describes a bare expression construct (pIRES2-DsRed2) with no tag whatsoever and does not qualify. L5 describes insertion of a stop codon after Gly155 to create a C-terminally truncated (ECD-only) construct; this is a truncation, not a tag insertion, and does not qualify under any ledger category. No ledger line reports a tag inserted at an extracellular position on full-length, membrane-anchored MOG. The large extracellular IgV domain (residues 30–155) and the single-residue extracellular loop at position 219 are both unaddressed by any qualifying insertion in the ledger. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag on full-length MOG (L1); C-terminus falls in the intracellular region (residues 230–247) per authoritative topology landmarks.
C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length MOG detected by anti-FLAG flow cytometry (L2); despite surface-display language in the paper, the canonical C-terminus is intracellular (230–247).
C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length MOG used for anti-FLAG affinity purification and surface display (L3); C-terminus is intracellular per topology.
